title: Restriction of a sheaf tensor product to an open immersion
statement: Let $j:Y\to X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $F,G$ be $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write restriction along $j$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] and tensor product as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There exists an isomorphism $(F\otimes G)|_Y\cong F|_Y\otimes G|_Y$ whose inverse, on every open $V\subseteq Y$, takes the pure tensor of restricted sections $s,t$ to the section corresponding to the pure tensor of their images in $F(j(V)),G(j(V))$ under the canonical restriction-section isomorphisms.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 17.16.4 (Tag 01CD), pullback along an open immersion

proof.text: By the sheaf tensor universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal], two morphisms out of a tensor product are equal if they agree on every pure tensor section. On Y, send sections s,t of the restrictions over V to their original pure tensor over j(V), regarded as a section of the restricted tensor product. The inverse structure-ring isomorphism makes this pairing O_Y(V)-bilinear; naturality of pure tensor sections makes it compatible with restriction. Extend it uniquely to c: F|_Y tensor G|_Y -> (F tensor G)|_Y.

On each open U of X, tensor the images of s and t under the units F -> j_*(F|_Y) and G -> j_*(G|_Y) of restriction adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Linearity and naturality of those units give a restriction-compatible bilinear pairing into j_*(F|_Y tensor G|_Y). Extend it by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] to b: F tensor G -> j_*(F|_Y tensor G|_Y), and take its adjoint d: (F tensor G)|_Y -> F|_Y tensor G|_Y.

Check c followed by d on pure tensor sections on Y. The adjoint d is restriction of b followed by the counit; the counit is restriction from j^(-1)(j(V)) to V. Compatibility of pure tensors with restriction reduces the result to the two left triangle identities, giving the original s and t. To check d followed by c, use injectivity of the restriction adjunction hom equivalence and pure tensor extensionality on X. Its adjoint sends a pure tensor to the tensor of the restrictions along j(j^(-1)(U)) -> U, which equals restriction of the original pure tensor. Thus both composites are identities. The isomorphism with hom d and inv c has the stated section formula by the construction of c.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01CD, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, open-immersion case: implemented using the tensor bilinear universal property (Modules on Sites, Section 03EK, display after Tag 0GMW) and the restriction/direct-image adjunction

lean.statement: theorem exists_restriction_tensor_comparison {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (F G : X.Modules) : ∃ e : (F ⊗ G).restrict j ≅ F.restrict j ⊗ G.restrict j, ∀ (V : Y.Opens) (s : Γ(F.restrict j, V)) (t : Γ(G.restrict j, V)), ((F ⊗ G).restrictAppIso j V).hom (e.inv.app V (tmulSection s t)) = tmulSection ((F.restrictAppIso j V).hom s) ((G.restrictAppIso j V).hom t)
